newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX May COB electricity settles up, May PV down.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX May COB electricity settles up, May PV down.

text.p: NYMEX May electricity futures settled mixed Wednesday as the complex struggled to find direction amid the lack of fresh fundamental news.
Continued absence of Bonneville Power Administration in the daily, peak market provided psychological support for California-Oregon Border (COB) futures, market sources said.

But the expected returns of the 1,221 Palo Verde 3 nuclear power unit near Phoenix, Ariz., and 1,070 MW San Onofre 2 nuclear unit in southern California to full output by this weekend put pressure on the Palo Verde (PV) contracts, brokers and traders said.
In the cash market, next-day power for firm, peak delivery at COB rose $1 to $14.00-15.00, while those at PV firmed 50 cents to $16.00-17.00.
May COB finished up 13 cents at $11.20 per megawatt hour (MWh) after traded between $11.10 adn $11.35. June COB ended up 10 cents at $11.50. Other active COB months settled down five to up 26 cents.

May Palo Verde (PV) futures finished down 27 cents at $15.04, near the day's low at $15.00 after posting a high of $15.25. June PV ended up five cents at $16.35. Other deferred PV contracts settled down seven to up five cents.

Despite bearish fundamentals in the West, rising cash prices and speculative interest in 1997 summer deliveries are expected to keep the complex in the upper end of its recent trading range, brokers and traders said.
Separately, the 1,073 MW Diablo Canyon unit 2 in central California remained shut after being taken off line last Saturday to repair a feedwater pump line.
Also, the 750 MW unit 2 at the Mohave coal-fired power plant in Nevada was shut last Saturday for planned maintenance. The unit is expected to stay down until May 11.
A 750 MW unit at the Navajo coal-fired plant in Arizona was heard still idled for repairs, which could take as long as two weeks to resume production.
The 1,158 MW WNP-2 nuclear plant in Washington was idled last Thursday for maintenance until summer.
Dry weather was expected in the Northwest through the end of the week with readings running three to six degrees Fahrenheit above normal.

In the Southwest, a low pressure system would bring cool and windy conditions with a chance of showers and mountain snow today into Friday. Temperatures were expected to drop five to 10 degrees below normal.
NYMEX estimated 357 COB and 304 PV contracts were sold, higher than 309 COB and 262 PV lots Tuesday.
